name: Chronic Infantile Neurological Cutaneous Articular Syndrome

clinicalPearls: CINCA (also called neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease, NOMID) is the most severe phenotype within the cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome (CAPS) spectrum, which also encompasses familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome and Muckle-Wells syndrome.

It presents in the neonatal period or early infancy with a migratory, non-pruritic urticaria-like (neutrophilic urticarial) rash, near-continuous systemic inflammation and characteristic facies (frontal bossing, saddle-shaped nose, macrocephaly).
The classic triad is chronic aseptic meningitis, a destructive arthropathy with bony overgrowth, and the urticarial rash.
A near-pathognomonic feature is epiphyseal and patellar bony overgrowth producing knobbly, deformed, contracted joints; this distinguishes CINCA from the milder CAPS phenotypes.

Neurosensory complications, including sensorineural hearing loss, chronic papilloedema with optic atrophy, and cognitive impairment, accrue over time and may become irreversible if treatment is delayed.
Interleukin-1 blockade produces a striking clinical and biochemical response and is the cornerstone of treatment.
Sustained, poorly controlled inflammation predisposes to secondary (AA) amyloidosis, chiefly affecting the kidneys.
A substantial proportion of patients with a classic phenotype but negative germline testing harbour somatic NLRP3 mosaicism, so deep sequencing may be required.
reference.pathophysiology: CINCA/NOMID arises from gain-of-function variants in NLRP3 (formerly CIAS1) on chromosome 1q44, which encodes cryopyrin, the sensor component of the NLRP3 inflammasome expressed predominantly in myeloid cells. Mutant cryopyrin assembles the inflammasome constitutively and inappropriately, driving unchecked activation of caspase-1, which cleaves pro-interleukin-1-beta into its active form; the resulting excess of IL-1-beta, together with IL-18, generates the systemic and organ-specific inflammation. Most disease-causing changes are heterozygous missense variants clustering in the central nucleotide-binding (NACHT) domain, and a considerable share of sporadic classic cases result from post-zygotic somatic mosaicism confined to a subset of leucocytes, which can render conventional germline sequencing falsely negative. The persistent IL-1-driven neutrophilic inflammation accounts for the urticarial dermatosis, the chronic aseptic leptomeningitis with raised intracranial pressure, cochlear and optic-nerve injury, and the disordered endochondral ossification responsible for the epiphyseal overgrowth.
additionalDifferentials: Familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome (mildest CAPS phenotype)
Deficiency of the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (DIRA) and other monogenic IL-1-mediated disorders
Neonatal sepsis or congenital (TORCH) infection with rash and meningeal signs
additionalInvestigations: NLRP3 gene sequencing, including deep next-generation sequencing of blood or affected tissue to detect somatic mosaicism
Acute phase reactants (C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate) and serial serum amyloid A monitoring
Lumbar puncture with opening pressure and cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing aseptic neutrophilic pleocytosis
Brain MRI seeking leptomeningeal and cochlear enhancement and ventricular enlargement
Formal audiometry and serial ophthalmological review with fundoscopy for papilloedema and optic atrophy
Skeletal radiographs demonstrating epiphyseal and patellar overgrowth
Screening for secondary amyloidosis with urinalysis for proteinuria and renal biopsy where indicated
redFlags: Progressive visual loss or intractable headache from raised intracranial pressure and chronic papilloedema
New or worsening sensorineural hearing loss
Proteinuria or falling renal function suggesting secondary amyloidosis
Persistent systemic inflammation despite therapy, prompting consideration of inadequate IL-1 blockade or unrecognised mosaicism
reference.prognosis: Historically CINCA/NOMID carried substantial morbidity and premature mortality from progressive neurosensory damage and amyloidosis. Early, sustained interleukin-1 blockade transforms the outlook, although neurological and sensory deficits already established before treatment are frequently irreversible.
pitfalls: A negative germline NLRP3 test does not exclude the diagnosis because of somatic mosaicism; deep sequencing of blood or affected tissue may be needed.
The rash is often misdiagnosed as ordinary allergic urticaria, yet it is typically non-pruritic, migratory and neutrophilic on biopsy.
Chronic aseptic meningitis may be mistaken for partially treated infective meningitis, delaying effective anti-IL-1 therapy.
The characteristic epiphyseal bony overgrowth is easily ascribed to another arthropathy rather than recognised as a diagnostic clue.
management: Interleukin-1 blockade with anakinra, canakinumab or rilonacept as the cornerstone of treatment, producing a striking clinical and biochemical response
Early and sustained interleukin-1 inhibition to prevent irreversible neurosensory damage such as sensorineural hearing loss and optic atrophy
Monitoring of C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate and serum amyloid A to guide therapy and detect subclinical inflammation and amyloidosis risk
Regular audiological and ophthalmological surveillance, including fundoscopy for papilloedema and optic atrophy, with management of raised intracranial pressure from chronic aseptic meningitis
Orthopaedic and physiotherapy support for the destructive arthropathy with epiphyseal and patellar overgrowth
Multidisciplinary care across rheumatology and immunology, neurology, audiology, ophthalmology and orthopaedics
Genetic counselling with NLRP3 testing, including for somatic mosaicism, and family screening
